field_product_items: • Transparent cone-shaped containers of 10 oz. containing 'thoughtfully handmade just for you Chicken Caesar Wrap with parmesan cheese, lettuce, and Caesar dressing' (Chicken Caesar Wrap with parmesan cheese, lettuce, and Caesar dressing, carefully made for you) with dates of 'best if consumed by' February 21, 23, and 25, and lot codes LPK1WA046, LPK1WA048, and LPK1WA050 printed on the label.
field_summary:
WASHINGTON, February 23, 2025 – LPK1, a company in Renton, Wash., is recalling approximately 303 pounds of ready-to-eat chicken Caesar wrap products due to misbranding and unreported allergens, announced today by the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS). The individual dressing packets contain fish (anchovies), a known allergen, that is not declared on the product label.

The ready-to-eat chicken Caesar wrap products were produced on February 15, 17, and 19, 2025. The following products are subject to recall:

  • Transparent cone-shaped containers of 10 oz. containing 'thoughtfully handmade just for you Chicken Caesar Wrap with parmesan cheese, lettuce, and Caesar dressing' (Chicken Caesar Wrap with parmesan cheese, lettuce, and Caesar dressing, carefully made for you) with dates of 'best if consumed by' February 21, 23, and 25, and lot codes LPK1WA046, LPK1WA048, and LPK1WA050 printed on the label.

The products subject to recall bear establishment number "P2276" inside the USDA mark of inspection. These items were distributed to vending machines in office buildings in Washington state.

The problem was discovered by the company during routine review of ingredient labels as part of its quality assurance process. The establishment subsequently notified FSIS that the product may contain fish (anchovies), which is not declared on the label.

No confirmed reports of adverse reactions have been reported due to consumption of these products. Any person with concerns about an illness should contact a healthcare provider. 

FSIS is concerned because some of the product may still be in vending machines at office buildings. Consumers who purchased these products are urged not to consume them and offices are urged not to serve them. These products must be discarded or returned to the machine owners.

FSIS conducts routine reviews of recall effectiveness to verify that companies that conduct a recall notify their customers of this and follow necessary steps to ensure the product is no longer available to consumers.

MEDIA with questions about the recall can contact Kristin Elder, Media Relations Specialist, H+K Strategies, at kristin.elder@hkstrategies.com. CONSUMERS with questions about the recall can contact Ryan Calbreath, Quality Assurance Manager, LPK1, at 925-457-6738 or in ryan.calbreath@compass-usa.com.

CONSUMERS who have questions about food safety can call the USDA's Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or send an email to MPHotline@usda.gov. CONSUMERS who need to report a problem with meat, poultry, or egg products can access the Electronic Consumer Complaint Form 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.
